Chart Geometry in Points

Source: R/layout.R
wjp_layout.Rd

wjp_layout() describes the geometry of a chart in points (1/72 inch), the unit of print layouts. Pass it to the layout argument of wjp_groupbars(), wjp_bars(), or wjp_dumbbells() to fix the label column, the 100% track, the row and header heights, and the margins, so the chart keeps the same measurements whatever the size of the device.

Usage

wjp_layout(
  label_width = NULL,
  label_gap = NULL,
  track_width = NULL,
  value_gap = NULL,
  value_width = NULL,
  row_height = NULL,
  bar_height = NULL,
  header_height = NULL,
  header_baseline = NULL,
  inset = NULL,
  margins = NULL
)

Arguments

label_width

Width of the label column.

label_gap

Gap between the label column and the start of the bars.

track_width

Width of a full (100%) bar.

value_gap

Gap between the end of the track (or of the bar) and the value labels.

value_width

Width reserved for the value labels.

row_height

Height of a data row (the pitch from one bar to the next).

bar_height

Height of a bar within its row.

header_height

Height of a group header row.

header_baseline

Baseline of the header text, measured from the top of its row.

inset

Space between the edges of the panel and the first and last rows: one value, or two values (top, bottom). Used by wjp_dumbbells() and wjp_groupbars() (row mode).

margins

Outer margins: one value, or four values in the order top, right, bottom, left.

Value

An object of class wjp_layout (a named list of numbers in points).

Details

With a layout, the chart is drawn with fixed panel sizes (see the panel.widths and panel.heights theme elements of ggplot2 >= 3.5.0) and its category labels are drawn as text layers in the label column, so no measurement of the text is needed. The resulting plot has a definite size, stored in attr(plot, "wjp_size") (inches), which wjp_save() uses when no width or height is given. Saving a plot with a layout at another size centers it on the canvas without changing its measurements.

Every argument is optional: the chart functions use their own defaults (those of WJP country reports) for the values left as NULL.

A horizontal chart with a layout is organized as follows, from left to right: margins[4], the label column (label_width), label_gap, the track (track_width, 0 to 100%), value_gap, the value column (value_width), and margins[2].

See also

wjp_save() to export a chart at its exact size.

Examples

# Geometry of the grouped bars of WJP country reports
report <- wjp_layout(
  label_width = 149, label_gap = 6, track_width = 250,
  value_gap = 5, value_width = 27,
  row_height = 15.5, bar_height = 13.5,
  header_height = 22, header_baseline = 17,
  margins = c(2, 0, 4, 0)
)
report
#> <wjp_layout> (points)
#>   label_width     149
#>   label_gap       6
#>   track_width     250
#>   value_gap       5
#>   value_width     27
#>   row_height      15.5
#>   bar_height      13.5
#>   header_height   22
#>   header_baseline 17
#>   margins         2 0 4 0
